[P4] Large-Injection LC Model and Transient Behavior: Exact Pull-In Solution, Lock Time, APF Amplitude Transient, and Pulling Spectrum

Prerequisites: paper_004 (APF definition [P4] Eq.(18)–(22), ISF/APF quadrature Eq.(26), augmented Adler Eq.(27)), lab_36 (the RRR-form exact solution of the in-lock Adler equation, critical slowing, cycle slips), injection_locking_noise (Part A first-order PLL, Part B beat frequency ωb\omega_bωb​ and the one-sided comb), phase_vs_amplitude_noise (amplitude recovery with τ0=2Q/ω0\tau_0=2Q/\omega_0τ0​=2Q/ω0​, OU process) | Next: the M:N / ILFD part of paper_004, lab_37 (simulations/lab_37_ilfd_lock.py, documented inside the paper_004 page), quadrature_and_coupled_oscillators.

paper_004 already covered the APF (amplitude perturbation function) definition of [P4], the ideal-LC ISF/APF quadrature, and M:N sub-/super-harmonic locking. This page collects what is left of [P4] Sec. III-E/F (the large-injection LC model) and Sec. V (transient behavior) and teaches it:

What this page answers:

  1. Why is the "amplitude-aware Adler" — Mirzaei's Generalized Adler's equation ([P4] Eq.(8)) — exactly the Γ~/(1+A)\tilde\Gamma/(1+A)Γ~/(1+A) model of [P4] (Eq.(13), (27))? In the large-injection lock range ωL=ωL0/1−a2\omega_L=\omega_{L0}/\sqrt{1-a^2}ωL​=ωL0​/1−a2​ (Eq.(9), (23)), is aaa equal to Iinj/IoscI_{inj}/I_{osc}Iinj​/Iosc​ or to Iinj/ImaxI_{inj}/I_{max}Iinj​/Imax​? Why does the model become "unbounded" for a≥1a\ge1a≥1?
  2. Where does the exact transient solution of the sinusoidal Adler equation come from? Why do the tanh⁡\tanhtanh of [P4] Eq.(31) (in lock) and the tan⁡\tantan of Eq.(33) (out of lock) look alike?
  3. How long does locking take? Is there a closed form? Why does an oscillator near the lock-range edge lock, but extremely slowly? What is the recipe behind the asterisk in [P4] Table I, "τp\tau_pτp​ from the slope of the lock characteristic"?
  4. What does the amplitude do during acquisition? How does the APF turn the phase transient into an amplitude dip/overshoot? When does the quasi-static assumption fail?
  5. Out of lock (pulling), is the large-injection beat frequency still Δω2−ωL2\sqrt{\Delta\omega^2-\omega_L^2}Δω2−ωL2​​? What does AM do to the pulling spectrum ("ISF + APF" vs "ISF Only" in [P4] Fig. 14(c))?

Physical intuition (conclusions first): the injected current simultaneously "pushes the phase" (ISF, tangential) and "changes the amplitude" (APF, radial). Once the amplitude changes, the ISF scales inversely with it (Γ~LC=Γ~/(1+A)\tilde\Gamma_{LC}=\tilde\Gamma/(1+A)Γ~LC​=Γ~/(1+A): a larger swing means the same charge pushes the phase less). That single feedback turns Adler's sin⁡θ\sin\thetasinθ into sin⁡θ/(1+acos⁡θ)\sin\theta/(1+a\cos\theta)sinθ/(1+acosθ) — when the injection is in phase with the oscillation (θ≈0\theta\approx0θ≈0) the amplitude is inflated, the restoring force weakens, and locking is slow; in anti-phase (θ≈±π\theta\approx\pm\piθ≈±π) the amplitude is drained, the restoring force strengthens, and the lock characteristic is pulled up — so the lock range is stretched from ωL0\omega_{L0}ωL0​ to ωL0/1−a2\omega_{L0}/\sqrt{1-a^2}ωL0​/1−a2​, and diverges as a→1a\to1a→1 through the nonphysical "zero amplitude" solution. As for the transient: after the tan half-angle substitution the sinusoidal Adler equation leaves a single quadratic; flipping the sign of its discriminant turns the in-lock tanh⁡\tanhtanh (exponential convergence at rate ωp\omega_pωp​) into the out-of-lock tan⁡\tantan (periodic slipping at the beat frequency ωb\omega_bωb​) — the same Pythagorean root ∣ωL2−Δω2∣\sqrt{\lvert\omega_L^2-\Delta\omega^2\rvert}∣ωL2​−Δω2∣​.

Scope of this page: advanced deep-dive ([P4] leftovers), not a core teaching chapter. Everything marked "✓ verified" below was checked word for word against the magnified original PDF: [P4] Eq.(5)–(9) and the Sec. III-B τ0=2Q/ω0\tau_0=2Q/\omega_0τ0​=2Q/ω0​ (p.2123), Eq.(13) (p.2124), Eq.(20)–(22) and footnote 7 (p.2126), Eq.(23) and the empirical θ∈[−110∘,110∘]\theta\in[-110^\circ,110^\circ]θ∈[−110∘,110∘] restriction (p.2127), Eq.(24)–(27) and the Fig. 8 caption (p.2128), Eq.(31)–(34), Table I and its asterisk note (p.2130), the Fig. 13 / Fig. 14 captions, Table II and the amplitude-conscious waveform (p.2131–2132), Eq.(35)–(38) (p.2132). Parts that are derived on this site and not in [P4] are labeled explicitly: the step-by-step derivation of Eq.(31)/(33) ([P4] only writes "one can show that [29]"), the closed-form beat frequency for large-injection pulling (Sec. 5.2), and the first-order amplitude-lag model (Sec. 4.3). External references are always flagged "(external reference, not among the site's 5 PDFs)" with the source checked word for word in [P4]'s bibliography.

[P4] immediately lists three limitations of this model (p.2123): it only handles sinusoidal injections; QQQ and IoscI_{osc}Iosc​ are hard to determine accurately because of parasitics, and modern integrated oscillators may not be modeled by the circuit of Fig. 1 at all; and the predicted lock range is symmetric, "which is not always the case [8], [12]". III-B thought experiment on the same page states the amplitude time constant explicitly: "we assume that any excess amplitude decays exponentially with a time constant of τ0=2Q/ω0\tau_0=2Q/\omega_0τ0​=2Q/ω0​ in between successive injections due to the energetics of the oscillator."

1.2 Effective ISF inversely dependent on amplitude, and the augmented pulling equation ([P4] Sec. III-C/E, p.2124 and p.2126 ✓)​

Γ~LC=Γ~1+A([P4] Eq.(13), p.2124)\tilde\Gamma_{LC}=\frac{\tilde\Gamma}{1+A}\qquad\text{([P4] Eq.(13), p.2124)}Γ~LC​=1+AΓ~​([P4] Eq.(13), p.2124)

The physics in the text of p.2124: "the oscillation amplitude controls the slope of the waveform (for a fixed oscillation frequency), and a steeper waveform corresponds to a proportionally smaller phase shift from the same injection of charge." Footnote 4 is honest: this inverse relationship holds exactly only when the state variables are mutually orthogonal (no AM-to-PM), which LC and Bose oscillators satisfy.

Amplitude deviation ([P4] Eq.(20), p.2126) and the augmented pulling equation (Eq.(21)):

A=1Tinj∫TinjΔ(ωinjt+θ) iinj(t) dtA=\frac{1}{T_{inj}}\int_{T_{inj}}\Delta\big(\omega_{inj}t+\theta\big)\,i_{inj}(t)\,dtA=Tinj​1​∫Tinj​​Δ(ωinj​t+θ)iinj​(t)dt dθdt=ω0−ωinj+1Tinj∫TinjΓ~(ωinjt+θ) iinj(t) dt1+1Tinj∫TinjΔ(ωinjt+θ) iinj(t) dt\frac{d\theta}{dt}=\omega_0-\omega_{inj}+\frac{\dfrac{1}{T_{inj}}\displaystyle\int_{T_{inj}}\tilde\Gamma\big(\omega_{inj}t+\theta\big)\,i_{inj}(t)\,dt}{1+\dfrac{1}{T_{inj}}\displaystyle\int_{T_{inj}}\Delta\big(\omega_{inj}t+\theta\big)\,i_{inj}(t)\,dt}dtd␀θ​=ω0​−ωinj​+1+Tinj​1​∫Tinj​​Δ(ωinj​t+θ)iinj​(t)dtTinj​1​∫Tinj​​Γ~(ωinj​t+θ)iinj​(t)dt​

[P4] calls this a "quasi-nonlinear" model: the nonlinearity hides only in the division of ISF by APF; each remains linear in the injection current. 4. Teaching (3): The Amplitude Transient During Acquisition (APF-Driven)​

4.1 Quasi-static amplitude: A(t)=acos⁡θ(t)A(t)=a\cos\theta(t)A(t)=acosθ(t)​

For an ideal LC under sinusoidal injection (Eq.(26)), [P4] Eq.(20) is simply A=12Iinj∣Δ1∣cos⁡(θ+∠Δ1)=acos⁡θA=\tfrac12 I_{inj}\lvert\Delta_1\rvert\cos(\theta+\angle\Delta_1)=a\cos\thetaA=21​Iinj​∣Δ1​∣cos(θ+∠Δ1​)=acosθ. It is an algebraic relation — the amplitude follows θ\thetaθ instantaneously (quasi-static). Combined with the amplitude-conscious waveform of p.2131:

vosc(t)∝[1+acos⁡θ(t)]cos⁡[ωinjt+θ(t)].v_{osc}(t)\propto\big[1+a\cos\theta(t)\big]\cos\big[\omega_{inj}t+\theta(t)\big].vosc​(t)∝[1+acosθ(t)]cos[ωinj​t+θ(t)].

Physics: at θ=0\theta=0θ=0 the injection current is in phase with the oscillation voltage → power is pumped into the tank → amplitude 1+a1+a1+a; at θ=±π\theta=\pm\piθ=±π anti-phase → power is drained → 1−a1-a1−a; at θ=±π/2\theta=\pm\pi/2θ=±π/2 quadrature → the phase is pushed but the amplitude is untouched (the time-domain version of the ISF/APF quadrature). Units: aaa dimensionless, AAA a relative amplitude deviation ✓.

4.2 Two amplitudes per detuning: the stable one is the larger​

In lock, sin⁡θ01+acos⁡θ0=ΔωωL0\dfrac{\sin\theta_0}{1+a\cos\theta_0}=\dfrac{\Delta\omega}{\omega_{L0}}1+acosθ0​sinθ0​​=ωL0​Δω​ has two roots for ∣Δω∣<ωL\lvert\Delta\omega\rvert\lt\omega_L∣Δω∣<ωL​ ([P4] p.2128: "two mathematical solutions for the phase θ\thetaθ and therefore also two possible oscillation amplitudes"); the stable root lies on the branch cos⁡θ0>−a\cos\theta_0\gt-acosθ0​>−a (Sec. 3.3, item 1), with amplitude 1+acos⁡θ0>1−a21+a\cos\theta_0\gt1-a^21+acosθ0​>1−a2 — this is the closed loop of solid (stable, large-amplitude) and dashed (unstable, small-amplitude) curves in the bottom row of Fig. 8, and the solid/dashed lines of lab_41 panel (c) are the same thing projected onto the lock characteristic.

4.3 Transient: dip → overshoot → settle, and when quasi-static fails​

Insert the θ(t)\theta(t)θ(t) of Sec. 2 into A=acos⁡θA=a\cos\thetaA=acosθ: if, when the injection is switched on, θ(0)\theta(0)θ(0) lies on the half circle with cos⁡θ<0\cos\theta\lt0cosθ<0 (anti-phase injection), the amplitude first drops below free-running (dip); as θ\thetaθ sweeps through 000 the amplitude shoots up to 1+a1+a1+a (overshoot); finally it settles at 1+acos⁡θ01+a\cos\theta_01+acosθ0​. lab_41 (b) uses θ(0)=−2\theta(0)=-2θ(0)=−2 rad, r0=0.5r_0=0.5r0​=0.5: the quasi-static AAA starts at −0.1987-0.1987−0.1987, peaks at +0.4775+0.4775+0.4775 (=a=a=a, at ωL0t=1.97\omega_{L0}t=1.97ωL0​t=1.97), and ends at +0.3519+0.3519+0.3519, an overshoot of 0.12560.12560.1256.

The premise of quasi-static is that the amplitude follows the phase "instantly" — but [P4]'s own APF definition Eq.(19) is the time integral of the decay function (Fig. 5(c): "the APF is equal to the area under the amplitude deviation impulse response"), with d(t)=e−t/τ0d(t)=e^{-t/\tau_0}d(t)=e−t/τ0​ for an ideal LC. So the amplitude is really the "drive acos⁡θ(t)a\cos\theta(t)acosθ(t)" passed through a first-order low-pass with time constant τ0\tau_0τ0​. Site extension (not in [P4], labeled illustrative):

τ0dAdt=acos⁡θ(t)−A,τ0 ωL0=a ⟹ a dAdτ=acos⁡θ−A(τ≡ωL0t).\tau_0\frac{dA}{dt}=a\cos\theta(t)-A,\qquad \tau_0\,\omega_{L0}=a\ \Longrightarrow\ a\,\frac{dA}{d\tau}=a\cos\theta-A\quad(\tau\equiv\omega_{L0}t).τ0​dtdA​=acosθ(t)−A,τ0​ωL0​=a ⟹ adτdA​=acosθ−A(τ≡ωL0​t).

The derivation is one step: A(t)=∫0∞acos⁡θ(t−τ′)τ0e−τ′/τ0 dτ′A(t)=\displaystyle\int_0^\infty\frac{a\cos\theta(t-\tau')}{\tau_0}e^{-\tau'/\tau_0}\,d\tau'A(t)=∫0∞​τ0​acosθ(t−τ′)​e−τ′/τ0​dτ′ (period-average Eq.(17) with D=Λ~ dD=\tilde\Lambda\,dD=Λ~d over the fundamental; what remains is the convolution of the slow envelope with d/τ0d/\tau_0d/τ0​, normalized so that a constant θ\thetaθ returns Eq.(20)'s A=acos⁡θA=a\cos\thetaA=acosθ); differentiate. Units: [τ0A˙]=[\tau_0\dot A]=[τ0​A˙]= s·(1/s) = dimensionless ✓. Quasi-static criterion: the phase-transient rate ωp\omega_pωp​ against the amplitude memory 1/τ01/\tau_01/τ0​ — ωpτ0=a ωp/ωL0≤a\omega_p\tau_0=a\,\omega_p/\omega_{L0}\le aωp​τ0​=aωp​/ωL0​≤a. Canonical a=0.4775a=0.4775a=0.4775, r0=0.5r_0=0.5r0​=0.5: ωpτ0=0.317\omega_p\tau_0=0.317ωp​τ0​=0.317 — not small. The lagged version in lab_41 (b): the dip only reaches −0.0443-0.0443−0.0443 (start A(0)=0A(0)=0A(0)=0: injection just switched on, amplitude not yet responding), peak +0.4577+0.4577+0.4577, peak delayed by 0.8850.8850.885 ns, the same final value +0.3519+0.3519+0.3519, and an essentially unchanged phase trajectory (both models at 0.742230.742230.74223 rad at ωL0t=24\omega_{L0}t=24ωL0​t=24). Conclusion: steady state and lock range are unaffected by the lag, but the height and timing of the transient amplitude peak are smeared by τ0\tau_0τ0​; for a≪1a\ll1a≪1 (weak injection) quasi-static is exact, while as a→1a\to1a→1 even quasi-static itself is in trouble (the unboundedness of Sec. 1.3). [P4] p.2128 further notes that nonlinear amplitude restoring (outside the linear APF model) is more prominent at large amplitudes — the second ceiling of the model on this page.

6. Worked Example (canonical numbers, one line per check)​

Lock time (θ(0)=0→θss−0.01\theta(0)=0\to\theta_{ss}-0.01θ(0)=0→θss​−0.01): ωL0Tlock=4.435\omega_{L0}T_{lock}=4.435ωL0​Tlock​=4.435 ⟹ 5.9135.9135.913 ns = 29.6 periods.

import numpy as np
from scipy.optimize import brentq
f0, qmax, Q, Iinj = 5e9, 1e-12, 10.0, 1.5e-3       # [Hz], [C], [-], [A]
w0 = 2 * np.pi * f0                                # [rad/s]
Imax = w0 * qmax                                   # [A]  I_max := w0*q_max,0  ([P4] fn.11, p.2130)
Iosc = Imax / Q                                    # [A]  I_osc = I_max/Q      ([P4] p.2132; w0*q_max,0 = Q*I_osc, p.2124)
a = Iinj / Iosc                                    # [-]  = (1/2)*tau0*Iinj/qmax = (1/2)*Iinj*|Delta_1|
print(round(Imax * 1e3, 2), round(Iosc * 1e3, 4), round(a, 4))          # -> 31.42 3.1416 0.4775
wL0 = Iinj / (2 * qmax)                            # [rad/s] ISF-only half lock range ([P3] Eq.(34)-(35))
wL = wL0 / np.sqrt(1 - a ** 2)                     # [rad/s] [P4] Eq.(9) = Eq.(23) at beta = 90 deg
print(round(wL0 / 2 / np.pi / 1e6, 2), round(wL / 2 / np.pi / 1e6, 2))  # -> 119.37 135.85
tau0 = 2 * Q / w0                                  # [s]  [P4] Sec. III-B, p.2123
print(round(tau0 * 1e9, 4), round(tau0 * wL0, 4))                         # -> 0.6366 0.4775
# (i) pull-in at Dw = 0.5*wL0: ISF-only [P4] Eq.(32) vs augmented slope recipe ([P4] Table I footnote)
r0 = 0.5
th_ss = np.arcsin(r0)                              # [rad] ISF-only locked phase
wp_isf = np.sqrt(1 - r0 ** 2)                      # [wL0] Eq.(32), N = 1
g = lambda th: np.sin(th) / (1 + a * np.cos(th)) - r0
th0 = brentq(g, -np.arccos(-a), np.arccos(-a))     # [rad] augmented locked phase (stable branch cos th + a > 0)
wp_apf = (np.cos(th0) + a) / (1 + a * np.cos(th0)) ** 2                 # [wL0] -Omega'(theta_0)/wL0
print(round(np.degrees(th_ss), 2), round(wp_isf, 4), round(np.degrees(th0), 2), round(wp_apf, 4))  # -> 30.0 0.866 42.53 0.6645
# (ii) lock time theta(0)=0 -> theta_ss - 0.01 rad from [P4] Eq.(31) (psi = theta + pi/2, alpha = tan(psi0/2))
eps = 0.01
psi0 = th_ss + np.pi / 2
alpha = np.tan(psi0 / 2)
T = (2 / wp_isf) * (np.arctanh(np.tan((psi0 - eps) / 2) / alpha) - np.arctanh(np.tan(np.pi / 4) / alpha))
print(round(T, 3), round(T / wL0 * 1e9, 3), round(T / wL0 * f0, 1))     # -> 4.435 5.913 29.6
print(round(1 / wL0 * 1e9, 3), round((1 + a) / wL0 * 1e9, 3))           # -> 1.333 1.97
# (iii) pulled at Dw = 2*wL: beat frequency, ISF-only Eq.(34) vs augmented closed form vs naive
r = 2 * wL / wL0
wb_isf = np.sqrt(r ** 2 - 1)                       # [wL0] [P4] Eq.(34), N = 1
R2 = 1 + (r * a) ** 2                              # [-]
S = np.sqrt(r ** 2 * (1 - a ** 2) - 1)             # [-]  -> 0 exactly at the augmented lock edge Dw = wL
wb_apf = R2 * S / (1 + r * a ** 2 * S)             # [wL0] site derivation (Sec. 5.2)
wb_naive = np.sqrt(r ** 2 - (wL / wL0) ** 2)       # [wL0] Eq.(34) with Eq.(9)'s wL plugged in
print(round(wb_isf * wL0 / 2 / np.pi / 1e6, 1), round(wb_apf * wL0 / 2 / np.pi / 1e6, 1),
      round(wb_naive * wL0 / 2 / np.pi / 1e6, 1))                        # -> 244.1 237.5 235.3

Full script: simulations/lab_41_large_injection_transient.py (depends on savefig from simulations/common/plot_utils.py and scipy.optimize.brentq; deterministic, no seed). Limitations: pedagogical toy (ideal-LC ISF/APF, not transistor-level); both the quasi-static APF and the first-order lag are linear amplitude models (no nonlinear restoring); (d) computes line amplitudes over integer-beat windows, and the −117.9-117.9−117.9 dB mirror line is the floating-point floor.

What remains external and is not done on this site: (i) [P4]'s original derivation of Eq.(31)/(33) is in Hong's Ph.D. dissertation [29] (this site proves them itself in Sec. 2); (ii) the original Generalized Adler derivation by Mirzaei et al. [11] and the lock-range derivations of [9], [10], [12] (this site uses only Eq.(7)–(9) as restated by [P4]); (iii) the geometric closed form of the pulling comb (Armand 1969); (iv) nonlinear amplitude restoring, AM-to-PM, and circuit-level (Spectre / PDK) verification — beyond this site's Level-1 equation-level model; the circuit-simulation values in Tables I/II can only be quoted, not reproduced.

What to remember​

  • Generalized Adler = ISF/(1+A): [P4] Eq.(27) equals Eq.(8) term by term; the bridge is the identity ω0qmax,0=QIosc\omega_0q_{max,0}=QI_{osc}ω0​qmax,0​=QIosc​ and a=Iinj/Iosc=12τ0Iinj/qmax,0=τ0ωL0a=I_{inj}/I_{osc}=\tfrac12\tau_0I_{inj}/q_{max,0}=\tau_0\omega_{L0}a=Iinj​/Iosc​=21​τ0​Iinj​/qmax,0​=τ0​ωL0​; lock range ωL0/1−a2\omega_{L0}/\sqrt{1-a^2}ωL0​/1−a2​ (Eq.(9) = Eq.(23) at β=90∘\beta=90^\circβ=90∘); unbounded for a≥1a\ge1a≥1 = the nonphysical zero-amplitude solution. ImaxI_{max}Imax​ governs linearity, IoscI_{osc}Iosc​ governs the amplitude effect — two different normalizations.
  • One quadratic, two signs: 2u˙=(ωL0+Δω)−(ωL0−Δω)u22\dot u=(\omega_{L0}+\Delta\omega)-(\omega_{L0}-\Delta\omega)u^22u˙=(ωL0​+Δω)−(ωL0​−Δω)u2, u=tan⁡(θ~/2)u=\tan(\tilde\theta/2)u=tan(θ~/2). In lock → tanh⁡\tanhtanh at rate ωp=ωL02−Δω2\omega_p=\sqrt{\omega_{L0}^2-\Delta\omega^2}ωp​=ωL02​−Δω2​ (Eq.(31)–(32)); out of lock → tan⁡\tantan at beat frequency ωb=Δω2−ωL02\omega_b=\sqrt{\Delta\omega^2-\omega_{L0}^2}ωb​=Δω2−ωL02​​ (Eq.(33)–(34)). The /2/2/2 in the tanh⁡\tanhtanh is half-angle bookkeeping; the decay rate is still ωp\omega_pωp​.
  • Lock time: Tlock=2ωp[artanh⁡−artanh⁡]≈τp[ln⁡(2sin⁡ψ0/ε)+… ]T_{lock}=\dfrac{2}{\omega_p}[\operatorname{artanh}-\operatorname{artanh}]\approx\tau_p[\ln(2\sin\psi_0/\varepsilon)+\dots]Tlock​=ωp​2​[artanh−artanh]≈τp​[ln(2sinψ0​/ε)+…]; r0=0.5r_0=0.5r0​=0.5, ε=0.01\varepsilon=0.01ε=0.01 gives ωL0T=4.435\omega_{L0}T=4.435ωL0​T=4.435 (identical to lab_36 digit for digit); diverges ∝(1−r)−1/2\propto(1-r)^{-1/2}∝(1−r)−1/2 at the edge.
  • The APF slows pull-in: ωpAPF=ωL0(cos⁡θ0+a)/(1+acos⁡θ0)2\omega_p^{APF}=\omega_{L0}(\cos\theta_0+a)/(1+a\cos\theta_0)^2ωpAPF​=ωL0​(cosθ0​+a)/(1+acosθ0​)2 (the slope recipe of Table I's asterisk); at band centre τp×(1+a)\tau_p\times(1+a)τp​×(1+a); the ideal-LC reconstruction of Table I(c) gives 17.0 (paper 17.4 / 16.9; only 12.2 without the APF).
  • Amplitude transient: A=acos⁡θ(t)A=a\cos\theta(t)A=acosθ(t) ⟹ dip → overshoot (to 1+a1+a1+a) → settle at 1+acos⁡θ01+a\cos\theta_01+acosθ0​; the stable solution is the large amplitude; quasi-static criterion ωpτ0≪1\omega_p\tau_0\ll1ωp​τ0​≪1, 0.317 in the canonical case — the lag smears the peak without changing the steady state.
  • Large-injection pulling: closed-form beat frequency ωbAPF/ωL0=R2S/(1+ra2S)\omega_b^{APF}/\omega_{L0}=R^2S/(1+ra^2S)ωbAPF​/ωL0​=R2S/(1+ra2S) (site derivation; returns to Eq.(34) as a→0a\to0a→0, S→0S\to0S→0 at the augmented edge); the AM factor =ejθ+a2+a2ej2θ=e^{j\theta}+\tfrac a2+\tfrac a2e^{j2\theta}=ejθ+2a​+2a​ej2θ raises k=0k=0k=0 (×1.30\times1.30×1.30) and k=2k=2k=2 (×1.49\times1.49×1.49), and the −30-30−30 dB mirror line comes from the non-Adler θ(t)\theta(t)θ(t) — the mechanism behind "ISF + APF" in [P4] Fig. 14(c).

  • phase_vs_amplitude_noise: amplitude recovery with τ0=2Q/ω0\tau_0=2Q/\omega_0τ0​=2Q/ω0​, the OU process and the flat-topped Lorentzian — the noise version of this page's lag model.
  • paper_003: generalized Adler, the lock characteristic, and the original definition ωp:=−Ω′(θ0)\omega_p:=-\Omega'(\theta_0)ωp​:=−Ω′(θ0​) ([P3] Eq.(38)–(40)).
  • tank_Q: QQQ, 2Q/ω02Q/\omega_02Q/ω0​ vs Q/ω0Q/\omega_0Q/ω0​, and where the canonical Q=10Q=10Q=10 comes from.
